methods.name: QLoRA
methods.paper_title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraConfig(target_modules='all-linear', ...) on a model loaded with BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type='nf4', bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True, bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16), after peft.prepare_model_for_kbit_training(model)
methods.formula_latex: h=\mathrm{doubleDequant}\big(c_1^{\mathrm{FP32}},c_2^{\mathrm{FP8}},W_0^{\mathrm{NF4}}\big)\,x+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BAx,\quad W_0^{\mathrm{NF4}}=q_{\mathrm{NF4}}(W_0)\ \text{frozen (blockwise, constants double-quantized)},\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{trained in BF16 (paged optimizer)}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: every linear layer of the transformer (attention and MLP); base weights stored as 4-bit NormalFloat
methods.structure: rank-r additive update BA on top of a frozen 4-bit NF4 (quantile-quantized, blockwise, double-quantized constants) base weight; storage dtype NF4, compute dtype BF16, so \Delta W factors through an r-dimensional space while W_0 lives on a 16-level grid
methods.mergeable_reason: BA merges exactly only into a dequantized 16-bit copy of W_0; merging and re-quantizing to NF4 adds fresh rounding error, so exact inference at the original 4-bit cost is not preserved.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 (LoRA default, A random), so the initial function is the quantized model \mathrm{dequant}(q_{NF4}(W_0)), not W_0: the quantization gap is left uncompensated at init (the gap LoftQ / LQ-LoRA / ApiQ close).
methods.key_idea: Backpropagate through a frozen 4-bit base model into LoRA adapters. Three memory tricks make this work: NF4 (a quantile data type that is information-theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights), double quantization of the scale constants, and paged optimizers. Together they let a 65B model be fine-tuned on one 48GB GPU.
methods.results_note: Fine-tunes a 65B model on a single 48GB GPU while matching 16-bit fine-tuning; Guanaco-65B reaches 99.3% of ChatGPT's score on the Vicuna benchmark after 24 hours on one GPU.

methods.name: QA-LoRA
methods.paper_title: QA-LoRA: Quantization-Aware Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraConfig(use_qalora=True, qalora_group_size=g) (default g=16; GPTQ-quantized linear layers only; PEFT does not implement the integer zero-point merge: merge/get_delta_weight raise NotImplementedError)
methods.formula_latex: \tilde W_0=\alpha\odot(\hat W-z),\ \hat W\in\{0,\dots,2^b-1\}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}}\ \text{(GPTQ, one }(\alpha_{j,l},z_{j,l})\text{ per output }j\text{ and input group }l=1..L);\quad h=\tilde W_0x+s\,BA\,\mathrm{pool}_L(x),\ \ \mathrm{pool}_L(x)_l=\textstyle\sum_{i\in\mathcal G_l}x_i,\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times L},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r};\quad \text{merge: } z'_{j,l}=z_{j,l}-s\,(BA)_{j,l}/\alpha_{j,l}
methods.trainable_params: r\,(L+d_{out}),\quad L=d_{in}/g
methods.locus: all linear layers of the LLM (attention and MLP projections); base weights group-wise INT2/3/4 quantized with GPTQ
methods.structure: low-rank update constrained to be constant on each input quantization group: \Delta W=s\,BAP with P\in\{0,1\}^{L\times d_{in}} the group-summation operator, so rank\le r and \Delta W lies exactly in the span of per-group zero-point shifts
methods.mergeable_reason: Because \Delta W is constant across the g inputs of every quantization group, it is absorbed exactly into the per-group zero-points, giving a pure INT-b model at the original inference cost.
methods.identity_at_init: LoRA-style zero initialization of one factor (B = 0), so training starts from the GPTQ-quantized model rather than from W_0.
methods.key_idea: QA-LoRA rebalances the degrees of freedom of quantization and adaptation. Quantization parameters become finer (group-wise) and the LoRA input becomes coarser (group-pooled), so every learned update is exactly a shift of the quantizer's zero-points. The adapter therefore merges into an INT-b model without loss.
methods.results_note: On LLaMA/LLaMA2 (7B-65B), INT4 QA-LoRA matches mixed-precision QLoRA and beats QLoRA+GPTQ on MMLU and commonsense QA. The margin widens at low bit-widths, e.g. +15.0% average commonsense accuracy over post-quantized QLoRA at 2 bits on LLaMA-7B.

methods.name: LoftQ
methods.paper_title: LoftQ: LoRA-Fine-Tuning-Aware Quantization for Large Language Models
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraConfig(init_lora_weights='loftq', loftq_config=LoftQConfig(loftq_bits=4, loftq_iter=1)) on the full-precision model; or replace_lora_weights_loftq(peft_model) on a bnb-4bit model (one LoftQ step only, LoRA weights replaced in place)
methods.formula_latex: \min_{Q,A,B}\lVert W_0-Q-BA\rVert_F:\ \ Q_t=q_N(W_0-B_{t-1}A_{t-1}),\ \ B_tA_t=\mathrm{SVD}_r(W_0-Q_t)\ (B_t=U_r\Sigma_r^{1/2},\ A_t=\Sigma_r^{1/2}V_r^{\top}),\ \ B_0A_0=0;\qquad h=(Q_T+BA)x,\ Q_T\ \text{frozen }N\text{-bit},\ A,B\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: all targeted linear layers (best with target_modules='all-linear'); quantized backbone (NF4/NF2 or uniform)
methods.structure: W_0 \approx Q + BA: an N-bit matrix plus the rank-r truncated SVD of the quantization residual, found by alternating quantization and SVD; fine-tuning then trains the rank-r part
methods.mergeable_reason: As with QLoRA, BA can be merged exactly only into a high-precision copy of the weight; merging into the N-bit Q requires re-quantization.
methods.identity_at_init: Approximate rather than exact: Q_T+B_TA_T approximates W_0. For T=1 the rank-r SVD of the residual W_0-Q_1 strictly lowers the error of QLoRA's Q_1+0 (Q_1 is exactly QLoRA's quantized weight); further alternations are heuristic (not guaranteed monotone). T=0 is QLoRA's zero-initialized adapter (paper Fig. 3).
methods.key_idea: LoftQ makes quantization LoRA-aware. It picks the quantized backbone and the LoRA initialization jointly, so the adapter starts out cancelling the quantization error. This matters most at 2-3 bits, where zero-initialized QLoRA often fails to train.
methods.results_note: In all reported experiments it is never worse than QLoRA ('We have not seen our approach performs worse than QLoRA') across DeBERTaV3 (GLUE, SQuAD, ANLI), BART (XSum, CNN/DM) and LLaMA-2 (WikiText-2, GSM8K). At 2 bits it gains over 8% on MNLI and more than 10% on SQuADv1.1.

methods.name: LQ-LoRA
methods.paper_title: LQ-LoRA: Low-rank Plus Quantized Matrix Decomposition for Efficient Language Model Finetuning
methods.formula_latex: \min_{Q\in\mathbb{Q}_{c},\,B,A}\big\lVert\sqrt{F}\odot\big(W_0-(Q+BA)\big)\big\rVert_F\ \ (F\equiv\mathbf 1\ \text{or diagonal empirical Fisher}):\ \ B^{(t)}A^{(t)}=\mathrm{SVD}_r(W_0-Q^{(t-1)}),\ \ Q^{(t)}=\mathrm{Quantize}_c(W_0-B^{(t)}A^{(t)}),\ Q^{(0)}=0;\ \ c=(\text{bits, block sizes})\ \text{per matrix from an ILP under a global bit budget};\quad h=(Q+BA)x,\ Q\ \text{frozen},\ A,B\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: all linear layers of the transformer, each with its own NF quantization configuration
methods.structure: robust-PCA-style low-rank-plus-quantized decomposition W_0 \approx Q + BA; Q uses a per-matrix mixed-precision configuration chosen by integer linear programming; data-aware variant uses a row/column-scaled (Fisher-weighted) SVD
methods.mergeable_reason: The low-rank component is high-precision and can be folded only into a dequantized copy of Q; folding into the quantized Q needs re-quantization.
methods.identity_at_init: Approximate: Q+BA is the alternating approximation of W_0 (stopped when the error rises). Since Q^{(0)}=0, the first low-rank component is the top-r SVD of W_0 itself, so the adapter starts on W_0's principal subspace rather than at zero.
methods.key_idea: Split each pretrained matrix into a fixed, easily quantized part and a trainable high-variance low-rank part. Integer linear programming then allocates bits across matrices to meet any target memory budget.
methods.results_note: Beats QLoRA and GPTQ-LoRA at matched bit budgets on LLaMA-2 (C4, OpenAssistant) and RoBERTa-large (GLUE). For example, 3.5-bit Fisher LQ-LoRA roughly equals 4.127-bit NF4 QLoRA, and a 2.75-bit LLaMA-2-70B (27GB) stays competitive with 16-bit.

methods.name: IR-QLoRA
methods.paper_title: Accurate LoRA-Finetuning Quantization of LLMs via Information Retention
methods.formula_latex: \hat W_0=\mathrm{NF}k\!\Big(\tfrac{W_0-\tau^{*}}{\mathrm{absmax}(W_0-\tau^{*})}\Big)\,\mathrm{absmax}(W_0-\tau^{*})+\tau^{*},\ \ \tau^{*}=\arg\max_{\tau}\ \mathcal H\big(\mathrm{NF}k((W_0-\tau)/\mathrm{absmax}(W_0-\tau))\big)\ \text{(blockwise search on } [\tau_0\pm\lambda\sigma],\ \tau_0=\mathrm{median};\ \text{scales and }\tau\text{ double-quantized)};\quad h=\hat W_0x+\alpha\,U_2(U_1(x)),\ \ U_1(x)=Ax+\beta_1\,\mathrm{avg}_r(x),\ \ U_2(u)=Bu+\beta_2\,\mathrm{rep}_{d_{out}/r}(u),\ \ \mathrm{avg}_r(x)_j=\tfrac{r}{d_{in}}\textstyle\sum_{i\in\mathcal G_j}x_i\ (r\text{ contiguous groups}),\ \ \beta_1,\beta_2\ \text{layer-wise learnable scalars}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+2
methods.locus: all linear layers of LLaMA/LLaMA2; NF2-NF4 or integer-quantized base
methods.structure: LoRA with parameter-free 'elastic' shortcuts: \Delta W=\alpha(B+\beta_2E)(A+\beta_1P), where P\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}} averages r contiguous input groups and E\in\{0,1\}^{d_{out}\times r} repeats each of the r entries d_{out}/r times; still rank \le r. Base is an entropy-calibrated NF-k quantizer with a per-block shift \tau
methods.mergeable_reason: The IEC shortcuts are linear and fold into the LoRA factors (and then into a 16-bit copy of the weight), but folding into the NF-k base requires re-quantization.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact relative to the quantized base: B = 0 and, in the official code, \beta_1=\beta_2=0 (the paper itself does not state their initialization), so the adapter is zero at step 0. The starting model is the ICQ-quantized one, not W_0.
methods.key_idea: View quantize-then-LoRA through information retention. Calibration Quantization (ICQ) maximizes the entropy of the quantized weights so they keep more information. The Elastic Connection (IEC) adds parameter-free pooling and tiling paths so LoRA can directly reuse the original features.
methods.results_note: Improves LLaMA/LLaMA2 at 2-4 bits over QLoRA and QA-LoRA, e.g. +1.4% MMLU for 4-bit LLaMA-7B over the prior state of the art, at only 0.31% extra training time.

methods.name: L4Q
methods.full_name: Low-rank adaptive Learning quantization for LLMs
methods.paper_title: L4Q: Parameter Efficient Quantization-Aware Fine-Tuning on Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W_{comb}=W_0+\alpha BA,\quad \tilde w=\mathrm{round}\Big(\mathrm{clamp}\big(\tfrac{W_{comb}-b}{s},Q_N,Q_P\big)\Big),\ \ W_q=\tilde w\,s+b,\quad h=W_qx;\ \ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ (A,B,s,b)\ \text{trained with STE};\ \ \tfrac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial B}=\alpha\big(\tfrac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial W_q}\odot\mathbb 1_{[Q_N,Q_P]}\big)A^{\top}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+2\,d_{out}\,d_{in}/g\ \ \text{(LoRA factors + one scale and bias per quantization group of size } g)
methods.locus: all linear layers (LLaMA 7B-33B, OpenLLaMA-3B, Mistral-7B)
methods.structure: learned-step-size quantizer composed after a rank-r additive update: W=Q_{s,b}(W_0+\alpha BA); custom backward reuses \partial\mathcal L/\partial W_q so no weight-gradient buffer is stored
methods.mergeable_reason: The deployed model is exactly the fully quantized W_q=Q_{s,b}(W_0+\alpha BA); no adapter or 16-bit branch remains at inference.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0, so training starts from the 'L4Q init' symmetric quantization of W_0 (scale s=\max(|\min W/Q_N|,|\max W/Q_P|), chosen to avoid clipping outliers), not from W_0 itself.
methods.key_idea: Put the LoRA update inside the quantizer rather than beside it, and train LoRA jointly with the quantization scale and bias. The result is a fully quantized model without QA-LoRA's constraints on the factors, at roughly LoRA's training memory.
methods.results_note: On LLaMA and Mistral models with instruction data, 4-bit and 3-bit L4Q is more accurate than decoupled quantize-then-fine-tune schemes and QA-LoRA, at inference speed comparable to other fully quantized models.

methods.name: PEQA
methods.paper_title: Memory-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Compressed Large Language Models via sub-4-bit Integer Quantization
methods.formula_latex: \hat W=\mathrm{diag}(s_0+\Delta s)\,\overline W_0,\quad \overline W_0=\mathrm{clamp}\big(\lfloor W_0/s_0\rceil+z_0,\,0,\,2^b-1\big)-z_0\ \ \text{(frozen integer codes)},\ \ s_0,z_0\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}};\ \ \text{only } s_0+\Delta s \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}\ \text{(per-channel; } d_{out}\,d_{in}/g \text{ for group size } g)
methods.locus: every linear layer of a weight-only (3-4 bit) quantized LLM
methods.structure: diagonal rescaling of the output rows of a frozen integer matrix: \hat W=\mathrm{diag}(s)\,\overline W_0 (group-wise: one scale per output row and input group); the integer codes never change
methods.mergeable_reason: The trained parameters are the quantization scales themselves, so the result is a standard quantized model with the same integer codes and kernels.
methods.identity_at_init: \Delta s = 0: the model starts as the RTN/OPTQ-quantized model whose scales s_0 minimize \lVert W_0-\hat W_0\rVert_F, so the starting point is close to but not exactly W_0.
methods.key_idea: Treat the quantization step sizes as the PEFT parameters. Freeze the integer codes and fine-tune only per-channel scales, so each task adapter is a tiny scale vector and the deployed model stays quantized.
methods.results_note: Scales to LLaMA-65B. After instruction tuning, sub-4-bit PEQA models recover or exceed their full-precision language-modeling, few-shot in-context and comprehension performance.

methods.name: ApiQ
methods.paper_title: ApiQ: Finetuning of 2-Bit Quantized Large Language Model
methods.formula_latex: \min_{Q,A,B}\ \big\lVert W_0X-(Q+BA)X^{q}\big\rVert_F\ \ \text{(layer-wise; block-wise: } \lVert\mathcal F(W_s,X)-\mathcal F(Q_s,A_s,B_s,X^{q})\rVert),\ \ Q=q_b(W_0;\gamma,\beta)\ \text{with learnable clipping }(\gamma,\beta)\ \text{via STE},\ X^{q}=\text{inputs from the already-quantized preceding layers};\ \text{then fine-tune } h=(Q+BA)x,\ Q\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{during fine-tuning}
methods.locus: all linear layers (or whole transformer blocks for ApiQ-bw); DeBERTa-v3, RoBERTa, Llama-2, Mistral
methods.structure: the same Q+BA shape as LoftQ, but fitted in activation space with calibration data, sequentially layer-by-layer or block-by-block so that quantization error does not accumulate with depth
methods.mergeable_reason: BA can be merged only into a high-precision copy; merging into the b-bit Q requires re-quantization.
methods.identity_at_init: Approximate: Q, A, B are calibrated so that the quantized layer or block reproduces the full-precision activations given the already-quantized inputs X^{q}; the model function is close to, not equal to, the original.
methods.key_idea: Initialize LoRA and quantize jointly by matching activations, not weights. Each quantized layer is fitted given its quantized inputs, so the adapter stops error propagation from shallow to deep layers, which is crucial at 2 bits.
methods.results_note: Attains the lowest activation error and the best fine-tuning results against QLoRA, LoftQ and LQ-LoRA across 2-4 bits on GLUE (DeBERTa-v3, RoBERTa) and on Llama-2/Mistral language modeling, arithmetic and commonsense reasoning, with the largest gains at 2 bits.

methods.name: EfficientQAT
methods.paper_title: EfficientQAT: Efficient Quantization-Aware Training for Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \text{Block-AP: }\min_{W,s,z}\lVert\mathcal F_{blk}(W_0,X)-\mathcal F_{blk}(Q_{s,z}(W),X)\rVert\ \text{block by block};\quad \text{E2E-QP: } \hat W=s\odot(\overline W-z),\ \overline W\ \text{frozen integers},\ \text{only step sizes } s \text{ trained end-to-end on the task loss}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}\,d_{in}/g\ \text{step sizes in E2E-QP (group size } g)
methods.locus: all linear layers of the LLM; 2-4 bit group-wise uniform quantization
methods.structure: two stages: block-wise reconstruction training of all weights plus quantization parameters, then end-to-end training of group-wise multiplicative step sizes only (diagonal-per-group scaling of a frozen integer matrix)
methods.mergeable_reason: Block-AP trains the latent weights together with step sizes and zero points and then rounds them to integer codes; E2E-QP trains only step sizes on those frozen codes. The output is a standard group-wise uniformly quantized model, with no adapter.
methods.identity_at_init: E2E-QP starts from the Block-AP-calibrated quantized model (step sizes from Block-AP); there is no exact identity with W_0, by design of quantization.
methods.key_idea: Make quantization-aware training feasible for 70B models in two stages. First, train all parameters block by block against a reconstruction loss. Then, end to end, train only the quantization step sizes, which is a PEQA-style parameter-efficient stage on a frozen integer model.

methods.name: LoQT
methods.paper_title: LoQT: Low-Rank Adapters for Quantized Pretraining
methods.formula_latex: h=\big(W_Q+s\,P_QB\big)x,\ \ W_Q=q_{NF4}(W),\ \ P=U_{[:,1:r]}\ \text{from}\ \mathrm{SVD}(\nabla_W\mathcal L)\ \text{(frozen, } P_Q=q_{NF4}(P)\text{; projector on the smaller side, shown for } d_{out}\le d_{in}),\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{trained},\ B_{init}=P^{+}(W-Q)\ \text{refined for up to 5 steps with } Q=q_{NF4}(W-PB);\quad \text{at } t\in\{T_i\}:\ W\leftarrow W_Q+sP_QB,\ \text{recompute }P,\ \text{re-quantize, re-init }B;\ \ T_{i}=\tau+\psi^{i}

methods.structure: one-sided low-rank adapter with a frozen gradient-derived projector, W=W_Q+sPB with P the top-r left singular vectors of \nabla_W\mathcal L; periodically merged into the NF4 weight and re-quantized at exponentially growing intervals

methods.key_idea: Realize GaLore's projected step as a trainable adapter. methods.name: GaLore
methods.paper_title: GaLore: Memory-Efficient LLM Training by Gradient Low-Rank Projection
methods.formula_latex: G_t=\nabla_W\mathcal L(W_t)\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}},\ \ P_t=U_{[:,1:r]}\ \text{of}\ \mathrm{SVD}(G_{t_0})\ \text{(refreshed every }T\text{ steps)};\ \ R_t=P_t^{\top}G_t\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ (M_t,V_t)=\mathrm{Adam}(R_t),\ N_t=M_t/(\sqrt{V_t}+\epsilon);\quad W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta\,\alpha\,P_tN_t\ \ \text{(all of }W\text{ trained; no adapter; shown for } d_{out}\le d_{in}\text{, else project on the right)}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{(full weight); optimizer state } 2r\,d_{in}+r\,d_{out}\ \text{vs. } 2d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{for Adam (for } d_{out}\le d_{in})
methods.locus: all 2-D weight matrices of attention and MLP blocks (embeddings / LM head usually kept on standard Adam)
methods.structure: each step's update lies in an r-dimensional left subspace: \Delta W_t=-\eta\alpha P_tN_t with P_t\in\mathrm{St}(d_{out},r) the gradient's top singular vectors; the subspace switches every T steps, so the accumulated \sum_t\Delta W_t is high-rank

methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: training starts at W_0 with no reparameterization; the projector is initialized from the SVD of the first gradient.
methods.key_idea: Put the low-rank structure on the gradient rather than the weights. Project each gradient onto a periodically refreshed top-r singular subspace, run Adam there, and project back. This gives full-parameter learning with LoRA-like optimizer memory.

papers.title: Gradient Descent Happens in a Tiny Subspace
papers.claim: After a short period of training, the gradient converges to a very small subspace spanned by the top few Hessian eigenvectors (about as many as there are classes) and stays there.
papers.relevance: Empirical basis for the 'dual' (gradient-side) PEFT view: if the gradient flow is effectively low-dimensional, projecting gradients (GaLore, Flora, APOLLO) or confining updates to low-rank parameter subspaces (LoRA) loses little. It also explains why projector refresh schedules matter.

papers.title: Adafactor: Adaptive Learning Rates with Sublinear Memory Cost
papers.claim: Adam's per-parameter second moment for a weight matrix can be replaced by its row and column sums (a rank-one factorization), cutting optimizer memory from O(nm) to O(n+m) with similar results. Update clipping and an increasing decay rate fix the resulting instability.
papers.relevance: The prototype of optimizer-state compression: factoring the second moment is the optimizer-side counterpart of factoring the weight update. It is reused directly by Flora and AdaLomo and shares a lineage with Adam-mini, APOLLO and GaLore-Adafactor.

papers.title: 8-bit Optimizers via Block-wise Quantization
papers.claim: Block-wise dynamic quantization, combined with a stable embedding layer, lets Adam and momentum states be stored in 8 bits with no loss in performance, removing about 75% of optimizer-state memory.
papers.relevance: Shows that optimizer states, not just weights, can be quantized. Its block-wise quantization (released in bitsandbytes) is the basis of QLoRA's block-wise NF4/double quantization and of 8-bit GaLore, and its 8-bit Adam is the baseline of GaLore 2. Paged optimizers were added later by QLoRA, not by this paper.

papers.title: Subspace Optimization for Large Language Models with Convergence Guarantees
papers.claim: GaLore does not always converge to a stationary point in the stochastic setting: SVD projectors become noise-dominated when the true gradient is small, as an explicit counterexample shows. It does converge with large batches or isotropic noise. GoLore, which samples random projections uniformly from the Stiefel manifold, provably converges at standard batch sizes.
papers.relevance: Gives the projector-selection morphism of gradient-side PEFT a precise convergence semantics. Data-dependent (SVD) projectors and data-independent (random) projectors behave differently, which explains the shift toward random or online projectors (Flora, APOLLO, Online Subspace Descent).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.11289 (He, 2024) confirmed; ICML 2025 (PMLR v267 he25i). Non-convergence counterexample (Thm 4), convergence with large batches or isotropic noise, GoLore sampling P from the uniform distribution on the Stiefel manifold confirmed.

papers.title: Revisiting Zeroth-Order Optimization for Memory-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning: A Benchmark
papers.claim: A benchmark of BP-free zeroth-order fine-tuning across five LLM families, three task difficulties and five fine-tuning schemes. It finds that task alignment and the forward-gradient method matter, and proposes block-wise descent, hybrid ZO/FO training and gradient sparsity to improve ZO fine-tuning.

notes: Scope: quantization-aware PEFT (QLoRA, QA-LoRA, LoftQ, LQ-LoRA, IR-QLoRA, L4Q, PEQA, ApiQ, EfficientQAT, LoQT) and gradient-side memory-efficient training (GaLore, GaLore 2, Q-GaLore, Flora, Fira, APOLLO, Online Subspace Descent, Adam-mini, MeZO, LOMO, AdaLomo, BAdam, LISA, LoRA-FA). Key structural observations for the category-theoretic site: (1) Duality theorem (exact). For a one-sided-frozen adapter W=W_0+PB with P frozen, dL/dB = P^T dL/dW, so any optimizer on B applies P*rho(P^T G) to W. LoRA-FA is therefore projected gradient descent with a fixed random right-projector, LoQT within one interval (no quantization, B_0=0) is exactly GaLore, and Flora is the resampled version. This is a clean natural correspondence between the parameter side (adapters) and the optimizer side (gradient projections). (2) The quantizer has two kinds of parameters, which give two dual PEFT families. Additive zero-points: QA-LoRA's group-pooled LoRA lands exactly in the zero-point space. Multiplicative scales: PEQA and EfficientQAT's E2E-QP, algebraically (IA)^3-type diagonal scaling. L4Q composes the quantizer after the LoRA update, W=Q_{s,b}(W_0+BA). (3) Quantization-aware initializations solve variants of min ||W_0 - Q - BA||: weight space for LoftQ and LQ-LoRA, with Fisher weighting in LQ-LoRA; activation space for ApiQ; entropy-maximizing quantizer for IR-QLoRA. QLoRA is the T=0 point, and with an identity quantizer LQ-LoRA reduces to PiSSA. (4) Mergeability: methods whose update lives in the quantizer's parameter space (QA-LoRA, PEQA, L4Q, EfficientQAT) merge into an integer model exactly. QLoRA, LoftQ, LQ-LoRA, IR-QLoRA and ApiQ merge exactly only into a 16-bit copy ('conditional'). Optimizer-side methods are trivially 'mergeable' because they write into W. Integration facts (not HF PEFT): GaLore (optim='galore_adamw'/'galore_adamw_8bit'/'galore_adafactor', '_layerwise'), APOLLO (optim='apollo_adamw', APOLLO-Mini via optim_args rank=1, scale_type=tensor), and LOMO/AdaLomo (optim='lomo'/'adalomo') are Hugging Face transformers Trainer optimizers. In HF PEFT: QLoRA via bitsandbytes + prepare_model_for_kbit_training; LoftQ via init_lora_weights='loftq' or replace_lora_weights_loftq; QA-LoRA via LoraConfig(use_qalora=True) (GPTQ only); LoRA-FA via peft.optimizers.create_lorafa_optimizer. PEFT also supports quantized bases via GPTQ, AQLM, EETQ, HQQ, torchao, INC (FP8) and Transformer Engine (plus AWQ in code), and VeRA, AdaLoRA and (IA)^3 with bnb. Uncertainties: IR-QLoRA's initialization of the learnable IEC scalars beta_1, beta_2 is not stated in the paper (the official code initializes both to 0). AdaLomo's Algorithm 1 prints u=g/v while the official implementation uses g/sqrt(v) (rsqrt); sqrt is written. LoRA-FA arXiv v3 (May 2026) adds the closed-form gradient correction (r/alpha)^2 (A A^T)^{-1}, which v1 (2023) lacked, and has no formal venue. GaLore 2 is a tech report with no confirmed code release (the GaLore repo only announces it). Fira's NeurIPS 2025 venue is confirmed by its NeurIPS 2025 poster page. Overlaps with other families (same ids used for merging): qlora, qa-lora, loftq, lora-fa (hf-peft / lora-core / init-rank), and badam, lisa (selective). The id 'flora-opt' deliberately differs from 'flora-batched' and 'flora-tucker' in other families. Relations reference ids from other families: lora, pissa, relora, ia3, prefix-tuning, lora-pro, riemannian-preconditioned-lora. Notable members omitted for low uptake or redundancy: Tensor-GaLore, GaLore-mini, LDAdam, SubTrack++, GoLore (treated as a theory paper), MeZO variants (Sparse-MeZO, HiZOO, MeZO-SVRG, SubZero, LoHO), QDoRA (blog only), CLoQ, RILQ, QuAILoRA, LR-QAT and VeLoRA (activation compression, covered in hf-peft).

No venue changed. Formulas were checked against paper PDFs/HTML and, where the paper is ambiguous, against official code; HF claims against huggingface/peft main @85be3f3 (2026-09-30) and the transformers optimizer docs. 44 corrections. Substantive: IR-QLoRA (IEC pooling/expansion operators, explicit absmax scale, beta_1=beta_2=0 at init from the official code), LoQT (trainable count r*max(d_in,d_out), iterative error compensation), Flora (momentum transfer only on resampling), LoftQ (init-gap claim qualified), QA-LoRA HF config (GPTQ only, no integer merge in PEFT), QLoRA HF config (BF16 compute dtype), EfficientQAT mergeability wording, AdaLomo sqrt sourced to code, 8-bit-optimizers lineage (paging is QLoRA's).
